Research and media

DIR project: AI and food in Bengaluru

For my DIR group project, I studied how AI is changing the way food is shown and sold in Bengaluru. My group visited eight food places, including a bakery, a pani puri stall, a biryani place, cafes and restaurants. We talked to owners, staff and customers, and always asked for permission first.

I shot the footage myself. I filmed menus, food, streets and short clips of people who agreed to be filmed. Then I edited everything into a video of about five minutes. I added subtitles for the Kannada and Hindi interviews, a voiceover and credits. After that, I put together the field notes diary, the consent forms and all the other documents.

In the field, I learned that not every place uses AI. Many menus were printed or painted by hand. One cafe made its whole menu with ChatGPT because it saves time. One stall owner did not even know what AI is. Some owners said they do not trust machines to cook. One customer preferred handmade menus and felt unsure about AI ones.

This project showed me that food is about people and their habits. AI can help sell food, but it cannot replace the hands that make it.

Analytics

Amul Kool Business Math Project

Amul Kool sells the most around Diwali. In this project, we played the role of a plant manager who had to make three decisions. How many bottles should we make each day? How much should we spend on ads each day? And is it worth spending ₹20 crore on a new bottling line?

We built a simple model. Selling more bottles lowers the price, while ads raise it. Demand also changes with the season, so we used a sine wave to show slow, normal and Diwali periods. Using partial differentiation, we found the best number of bottles and the best ad spend for each season. Both go up during Diwali.

Next, we used the chain rule to see how these choices and profit change through the year. Profit and ad spend grow fastest just before Diwali.

Finally, we used integration to find the present value and NPV of the new bottling line, with a 1% monthly discount rate. This showed whether the investment is worth it and how long it takes to pay back.

Our model assumes a perfect sine curve, no competition and example numbers. It taught me how maths can turn a business problem into a clear decision.

Communication

LLR project: rebranding Captain G. R. Gopinath 

For my LLR project, I rebranded the persona of Captain G. R. Gopinath, the founder of Air Deccan. I studied his life through three ideas from rhetoric: ethos (trust), pathos (emotion) and logos (logic).

I made the whole presentation myself. I picked the boarding pass theme and designed each slide on my own. I added the photos, icons, stickers, text boxes and shapes one by one, and I chose the colours and fonts so the slides matched. I also wrote the script and put everything together so the slides and the speech worked as one story.

Here is what I found. Ethos came from his army years, his farming life and his title “Captain”. Pathos came from his village roots and from Air Deccan’s one-rupee fares, which made first-time flying feel possible. Logos came from the plan to charge less and fill more seats. But I also learned that low fares alone are not enough, because the airline still needed strong finances.

My main finding was a gap. His roles as soldier, farmer, entrepreneur, author and political candidate did not always feel like one brand. So I created “Gopinath 2.0” with the tagline “Grounded in soil. Cleared for takeoff.” It links his roots with his big dreams.
